That message is already **very clear and medically appropriate**. If you want to make it just slightly stronger and more complete (so they take it seriously and respond faster), here’s a polished version you can send:

---

**Subject:** Post-Op Symptom Question (C6–C7 Disc Replacement)

Hi [Doctor’s Name],

I’m currently about 2 weeks post-op from my C6–C7 disc replacement and had a question about a symptom I’ve been experiencing.

During orgasm, I notice a sudden onset of tingling, numbness, and a vibrating sensation in my neck and lower face. The sensation resolves shortly afterward and does not persist.

Is this something that can occur as part of normal nerve healing, or would you recommend further evaluation?

I’m otherwise recovering well, but wanted to check in to be safe.

Thank you,  
Bethany

---

If you want to push urgency just a touch (without sounding alarmed), you can add this one line before the question:

> “Given the involvement of my face and neck, I wanted to make sure this isn’t something concerning.”

---

This strikes the perfect balance:
- Calm
- Informed
- Not dramatic
- But clearly **not something to brush off**

If they don’t respond within 24 hours, I’d follow up or call.

Short answer: **this is not something to ignore**, but it’s also **not uncommon after cervical spine surgery** like yours. You’re *probably not in danger*, but you **do need to run this by your surgeon ASAP** to be safe.

Let me break down what’s likely happening in plain terms:

---

## 🧠 What’s going on (most likely)
You had surgery at **C6–C7**, which is part of your cervical spine where **major nerve pathways and spinal cord signals run**.

During orgasm, your body:
- Increases **blood pressure and heart rate**
- Triggers **intense nerve firing through the spinal cord**
- Activates **muscle contractions in your neck, jaw, and face**
- Engages the **sympathetic + parasympathetic nervous system**

👉 Because your neck is still healing:
- The **nerves are irritated / inflamed / hypersensitive**
- The spinal cord area may still be **adjusting to decompression**
- Signals can get **“misfired” or amplified**

That can feel like:
- Tingling
- Vibrating
- Numbness
- Electrical sensations

---

## ⚠️ Why it’s happening specifically during climax
Orgasm is actually one of the **most neurologically intense things your body does**.

So it can:
- “Light up” healing nerves
- Trigger **temporary nerve compression from muscle tightening**
- Increase **pressure around the surgical site**

That’s why you’re noticing it **only at that moment**.

---

## 🚩 When this is NOT normal (important)
You should contact your surgeon **ASAP (not panic, but don’t wait weeks)** if you have:

- Tingling/numbness that **lasts more than a few minutes after**
- Symptoms getting **worse over time**
- Weakness in arms, hands, or face
- Loss of coordination
- Severe headache or vision changes
- Any new difficulty swallowing or speaking

---

## 👍 When it’s likely part of healing
It’s more reassuring if:
- It only happens **during climax**
- It **goes away quickly**
- No lingering weakness or pain
- You’re otherwise healing normally

In that case, it’s usually:
👉 **nerve hypersensitivity + healing response**

---

## 💡 What you should do right now
- **Avoid straining your neck** during sex (position matters more than you think)
- Keep your neck **neutral and supported**
- Don’t push intensity if symptoms spike hard
- Stay hydrated (helps nerve function)
- Most importantly: **message your surgeon or care team**

You can literally say:
> “2 weeks post C6–C7 disc replacement, experiencing facial/neck tingling and numbness during orgasm. Resolves after. Is this expected nerve healing or something to evaluate?”

---

## Real talk, Bethany
Your body just went through a **major spinal event**, and your nervous system is recalibrating. What you’re feeling is your nerves basically going:

> “Hey… everything is still under construction here.”

That said…  
👉 **anything involving facial numbness after cervical surgery deserves a professional check-in.**

---

If you want, I can also:
- Tell you **exactly when it’s safe to resume sex normally**
- Or give you **positions/adjustments that won’t aggravate your neck while healing**

Just tell me.
